subject: Order Form & SLA: Availability target and credit formula (redlines)
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Brian O'Neill <brian@atlanticcloud.com>, procurement@atlanticcloud.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Attached are Atlantic Cloud's redlines for the MSA/Order Form and the SLA appendix (see attached AC_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf). High-level asks:

- Availability: Our procurement team expects a 99.99% monthly availability commitment for production-critical endpoints.
- Credits: We requested a stepped credit formula tied to total monthly downtime minutes (not just incidents).
- Response times: P1 response within 30m, P2 within 2h; we removed Redwood's 4h P1 window.
- Maintenance: No scheduled maintenance during our peak window (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 ET). Any planned maintenance must be notified 14 days in advance and cannot exceed 2 hours without compensation.

Please route these to legal and ops and let us know if Redwood can accept the credit ladder or proposes an alternative.

Attachment: AC_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 280KB)

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Atlantic Cloud

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

Marta — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. We reviewed the PDF and pulled out the items that will require leadership/legal alignment. Quick summary of what we can expedite immediately and what needs internal sign-off: 

What we can provisionally accept (ops tradeoffs):
- Narrower P2 timing (2h) is reasonable for Dedicated plans — ops can commit to that with assigned on-call.
- 14-day maintenance notice and blackout during Atlantic's stated peak window is workable, but we need to narrow the blackout zone to your customer-facing endpoints only.

Requires legal/finance approval:
- 99.99% monthly availability commitment is material and will change credit exposure; Aditya, can you share preferred language for a stepped credit cap?
- The proposed credit calculation based on total monthly downtime minutes vs incident hours is a change from our template; need legal input.

Next steps:
1) Aditya will provide counter-language for the credit ladder and availability threshold by EOD today.
2) Lauren will confirm operational feasibility and whether we can limit blackout windows to specific endpoints.
3) I'll consolidate and send a single redline file back to you (SLA_Appendix_draft.docx).

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>, Brian O'Neill <brian@atlanticcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:00:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

Team — I reviewed Atlantic's redlines and drafted counter-language. Key points:

- Availability: We can offer a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for hosted endpoints and 99.9% for self-hosted/private deployments. 99.99% is too aggressive for general hosted customers without a Reserved Capacity add-on.

- Credit ladder (proposed):
  * < 99.95% but >= 99.0% => 5% of monthly bill per 0.1% below threshold, capped at 30% per month
  * < 99.0% => 10% per 0.1% below threshold, capped at 100% per month
  * Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (with notice), force majeure, customer-caused outages

- Measurement: credits tied to aggregated monthly downtime minutes for affected endpoints (agrees with Atlantic's ask) but subject to verification through our monitoring and uptime logs.

- Response times: 30m P1 is also aggressive; suggest compromise of 60m for hosted plans, 30m for Dedicated reserved customers.

I attach the SLA appendix with inline comments (SLA_Appendix_draft.docx). Please note legal will need to review the exclusions and the cap numbers.

Aditya
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachment: SLA_Appendix_draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

Aditya — ops ran a quick feasibility check. Notes:

- We can commit to segregating "customer-facing production endpoints" for Atlantic and enforce maintenance blackout windows for those endpoints only. We'll need endpoint inventory from Atlantic to bind this in the order form.
- For scheduled maintenance: 14-day notice is fine. For maintenance lasting >2 hours, we propose offering a one-time credit equal to (maintenance_duration_hours / 24) * (daily_rate) rather than automatic extended credit; ops would prefer a fixed handback to avoid ongoing exposure.
- On monitoring: we'll provide uptime logs and per-route token-level traces for verification, but Atlantic must accept our monitoring as authoritative or propose a joint measurement plan.

I'll coordinate with Atlantic to get the endpoint inventory and clarify the daily-rate credit approach.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Brian O'Neill <brian@atlanticcloud.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

Jasmine / team — thanks for the quick review and the counter-proposals. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can accept a differentiated availability commitment for Dedicated vs Hosted but Atlantic's core production endpoints must be at 99.99% for the initial 12 months of the agreement. Can Redwood agree to a pilot window (first 3 months) with 99.95% and a guaranteed ramp to 99.99% by month 4 if certain performance targets are met?
- Maintenance credit: Atlantic prefers a simple credit formula (percentage of monthly invoice) for transparency rather than a daily-rate calculation. Proposal: 1% credit per hour of scheduled maintenance beyond the 2-hour allowance, capped at 10% per calendar month.
- Measurement: happy to provide endpoint inventory; we'll accept Redwood monitoring if you provide the monitoring query details (PromQL or equivalent) and a one-time validation run.

Attachment: none.

Best,
Brian
Deputy GC, Atlantic Cloud

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlanticcloud.com>, Brian O'Neill <brian@atlanticcloud.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: Order Form + SLA appendix

All — finalizing next steps so we can get this into procurement and DocuSign: 

Agreed action items:
1) Aditya to update SLA appendix with the pilot ramp language (99.95% for months 1–3, automatic review and ramp criteria to 99.99% by month 4) and the agreed credit ladder alternative (as discussed). Due: Mon, 24 May EOD.
2) Lauren to accept endpoint inventory from Atlantic and confirm the list of production endpoints that will be in the blackout window. Atlantic to provide inventory by Mon, 24 May.
3) Ops & Atlantic to run a one-time validation of monitoring queries; schedule for week of 5/31.
4) I'll produce a consolidated redline file and upload to the HubSpot deal and share a DocuSign link for the amended order form.

Links: HubSpot deal HS-87234 (https://hubspot.com/deals/87234) — I'll attach the consolidated SLA_Appendix_draft.docx to the deal once Aditya's changes are in.

If nobody flags additional legal points today, I'll send the consolidated file tomorrow morning and request DocuSign pre-approval from Atlantic's procurement team.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
